newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FALDO SAYS IT'S TOO EARLY FOR TIGER TIME AT THE MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO SAYS IT'S TOO EARLY FOR TIGER TIME AT THE MASTERS.

text.p: Nick Faldo thinks the world of Tiger Woods, but the defending Masters champion figures it's early to expect great things from the young American at Augusta National just yet.

Faldo, a three-time winner of the coveted green jacket, pronounced himself ready for another title assault, pleased with his current putting form after devoting two hours a day to correct an alignment fault.

Asked what he thought about the chances for victory for the 21-year-old Woods, tabbed by some pundits as a favourite to become the youngest Masters champion in his third visit to Augusta, the Briton hedged his comments.
"What he did as an amateur was phenomenal," Faldo said about the winner of an unprecedented three successive U.S. Amateur titles. "What he's done so far as a pro is phenomenal."
Faldo, however, believes the spectacular burst that saw Woods win three times on the U.S. PGA Tour in his first nine tournaments would be hard to replicate at the Masters.

"I think there's a learning curve playing at Augusta," said Faldo, who figures it took him about six Masters before he was ready to mount a serious challenge in the traditional opening major of the golf season.

"The experience you get from playing over the years at Augusta National is important and the discipline you learn about when to be aggressive and when not, when you just want to make a par and walk on."
Faldo would not rule out a Woods win but cautioned against great expectations from golf's most exciting newcomer.
"It's not impossible," he said about the long-hitting Woods' chances. "But I think experience helps here. I wouldn't be shocked but it's his early days."

Faldo, who also has three British Open crowns to his credit, won last year in a remarkable turnabout on the final day when he shot 67 to make up a six-stroke deficit against his playing partner Greg Norman, who blew to a 78 and lost by five.
The defending champion said he wished Norman well this year. "If he's there and can do it again, then good luck to him."
The Briton was asked if he would like to be able to present the green jacket this time to Norman, or to any other player in particular.
"No," he said. "I want it to stay in my wardrobe. It's as simple as that."
